titlePlain: Case Study: Catching a Slow Data
subtitle: Lesson 31 · Capstone: Building a Layered Threat Detection Program

eyebrow: Nine days, three megabytes at a time

steps.label: NetFlow deviation
steps.sub: a new destination, contacted on a suspicious schedule

steps.label: Threat intel hit
steps.sub: the destination IP is a listed IOC

steps.label: EDR telemetry
steps.sub: a disguised process is making the connections

eyebrow: Signal 1 — the baseline, not the volume
code:
Normal:  <5 MB/day, known SaaS destinations only
Now:     ~2-3 MB every 25-30 min, to a destination
         this host has never contacted before
caption: No single transfer trips a threshold — the pattern itself is what's new.

eyebrow: Signal 3 — the process tree tells the story
code:
WINWORD.EXE
  -> cmd.exe
       -> svch0st.exe   (temp folder, not System32)
caption: A document opened nine days ago spawned the shell that spawned the disguise.

eyebrow: Once all three signals line up

steps.label: Isolate the host
steps.sub: EDR cuts network access, evidence stays intact

steps.label: Block the destination
steps.sub: the flagged IP gets blocked at the perimeter NGFW

steps.label: Sweep the IOC
steps.sub: check every other host's flow and EDR history
